# The required-check set — the single source of truth for "may this merge?".
#
# WHY A FILE: GitHub's own required-status-checks live in branch protection /
# rulesets, and BOTH are 403 on this repo (private on a free plan:
# "Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this
# feature"). So there is no server-side gate to configure. This file plus
# `just pr-gate <n>` (scripts/pr_gate.py) is the gate: run it before merging.
# The moment protection becomes available, the `required*` lines below are
# exactly the list to paste into it — no re-derivation.
#
# Format:  <tier>  <workflow>/<job>   [# note]
#   required         must exist and pass
#   required-if-run  must pass IF it ran — for PATH-FILTERED jobs, whose
#                    absence is correct on an unrelated PR (the same case that
#                    makes path-filtered required checks hang a real ruleset)
#   advisory         reported, never blocks — a tier serving probation
#
# "DID NOT RUN" HAS TWO SHAPES and the tier is what decides, not the shape: a
# workflow-level `paths:` filter makes a check ABSENT (`kind/cluster-tests`),
# while `ci.yml`'s `changes` job makes one SKIPPED. `pr_gate.py` treats them
# identically — a `required` line fails on either. So a job that can be
# filtered out MUST be `required-if-run`, and the line MUST move in the same
# commit as the filter, or the gate reds on a correct skip.

# The one check that always runs (`ci.yml`'s `changes` job computes the path
# filters every other job is gated on). It is `required` because everything
# below is now skippable: without an unconditional anchor, a docs-only PR would
# pass this gate having validated literally nothing, and a broken filter
# expression would report green.
required         ci/changes             # the path-filter decision itself

# Path-filtered by `changes` since git-bug 6729fc2 — a UI-only PR correctly
# skips the Rust tier, a Rust-only PR correctly skips the UI tier, and a
# Rust-or-UI PR always runs the contract gate. On a push to MAIN nothing is
# filtered, so trunk still runs all three.
#
# `ci/test` and `ci/coverage` were ONE job as of git-bug b69c286 — the two ran
# the same 1,056 tests, and `cargo llvm-cov nextest` fails on a red suite, so
# the merged job reports a strict superset. If you are here because a check
# named `ci/test` went missing: it is `ci/test-and-coverage` now.
required-if-run  ci/test-and-coverage   # workspace nextest under llvm-cov, real PG + MinIO, then the ratchet
required-if-run  ci/openapi-drift       # committed spec + generated client + tsc
required-if-run  ci/ui-tests            # UI no-DOM vitest suites

# Promoted off probation 2026-07-25. Nine runs, one failure — and that failure
# was the harness `.expect()`ing a transient poll error the engine is designed
# to retry ("workspace: broken pipe"), fixed in the same commit. No product
# flake was ever observed, so it graduates.
required-if-run  kind/cluster-tests     # live-cluster executor tier

# Probation until ~2026-08-08 (wired 2026-07-25 — needs a track record first).
# Promote by moving this line up and deleting `continue-on-error` in ci.yml.
advisory         ci/ui-e2e              # 2 Playwright specs over mock mode
